correctness.rationale: For every integer n at least 3, the disjoint families of adjacent pairs at even starts and separated pairs at positions (4j+1,4j+4) have floor(n/2)+floor((n-1)/4) words. Direct enumeration of the at most three weight-two outputs and one/two weight-one outputs establishes distinctness across families and between blocks. Independently, all n-1 weight-one deletion outputs plus ceil((n-1)/2) adjacent-weight-two outputs induced by an edge cover of the path on adjacent input-pair labels hit every possible weight-two input deletion ball at least twice. Disjointness forces twice the code size to be no greater than this output count; integer rounding gives exactly floor((3n-2)/4). Actual standalone paths verify.py and verify.cpp checked the claimed construction, dual covering and small exact clique maxima. No computation is used to extrapolate to arbitrary n.

value.rationale: The weight-two class is a canonical first nontrivial sparse input-composition layer in deletion coding, and constant-weight layering is an explicit research strategy in the inspected 2012 primary source. The exact all-length maximum is not already determined by prior graph colorings, requires a nontrivial block-separated construction and a tight deletion-output obstruction, and can guide exact sparse deletion code design. It resolves a natural unknown graph independence invariant for every length, not an arbitrary finite slice or routine table extension. It does not claim practical rate for unrestricted codes or any unsupplied downstream theorem.
